security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel context-switch or trap handler writes to the now-WPRI bits 24 (SPTTCD) or 42 (MPTTCD) in mstatus/sstatus, or kernel relies on mret/sret to restore a TTCD state that no longer exists — causing silent corruption of adjacent fields if hardware repurposes these bits.
security_spec.summary: Zitagelide removal reclaims mstatus[42] and sstatus[24] as WPRI; kernel must not touch these bits — any stale save/restore of the now-nonexistent TTCD state would corrupt CSR fields across context switches or VM exits.

findings.finding: No CSR bit definitions exist for SPTTCD (bit 24), MPTTCD (bit 42), or any TTCD-related field in sstatus/mstatus. The zitagelide extension is fully absent from the CSR bit definitions in both the main kernel header and the tools/ copy. The only bit-24 use is SR_VS_CLEAN_THEAD (0x01000000) for XTheadVector, an unrelated vendor extension.
findings.snippet:
#define SR_FS    _AC(0x00006000, UL) /* Floating-point Status */
#define SR_VS    _AC(0x00000600, UL) /* Vector Status */
#define SR_XS    _AC(0x00018000, UL) /* Extension Status */
/* No SPTTCD, MPTTCD, TTCD, or zitagelide definitions anywhere */

findings.finding: Trap entry reads CSR_STATUS via csrrc clearing only SR_SUM|SR_FS_VS|SR_ELP. Bits 24 and 42 are NOT in the clear mask, so they pass through unchanged as opaque bits in the save/restore cycle. The saved status is stored in pt_regs->status and restored verbatim at line 301 via csrw CSR_STATUS. No explicit manipulation of TTCD bits occurs.
findings.snippet:
li t0, SR_SUM | SR_FS_VS
#ifdef CONFIG_64BIT
li t1, SR_ELP
or t0, t0, t1
#endif
REG_L s0, TASK_TI_USER_SP(tp)
csrrc s1, CSR_STATUS, t0

findings.finding: Trap return restores CSR_STATUS from pt_regs->status as a full opaque write, then executes sret. No TTCD-specific logic. The sret instruction does not rely on any TTCD state restoration semantics since the kernel never configures TTCD behavior.
findings.snippet:
csrw CSR_STATUS, a0
csrw CSR_EPC, a2
REG_L x1,  PT_RA(sp)
...
sret

findings.finding: Context-switch __switch_to reads CSR_STATUS to save the SUM bit state, then conditionally sets SR_SUM into CSR_STATUS via csrs. Does not read, write, or manipulate bits 24 or 42. The full status (including any opaque bits) was already saved in pt_regs->status by the trap entry path.
findings.snippet:
csrr  s0, CSR_STATUS
REG_S s0, TASK_THREAD_SUM_RA(a3)
...
REG_L s0,  TASK_THREAD_SUM_RA(a4)
li    s1,  SR_SUM
and   s0,  s0, s1
csrs  CSR_STATUS, s0

findings.finding: KVM VCPU switch correctly saves and restores the full SSTATUS CSR via csrrw atomic swap. The guest sstatus is loaded from guest_csr and host sstatus is saved. Bits 24/42 are treated as opaque fields passed through save/restore. Neither the host nor guest paths write specific values to TTCD bit positions.
findings.snippet:
SAVE_HOST_AND_RESTORE_GUEST_CSRS:
  REG_L t0, (KVM_ARCH_GUEST_SSTATUS)(a0)
  csrrw t0, CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  ...
  REG_S t0, (KVM_ARCH_HOST_SSTATUS)(a0)

findings.finding: VCPU load writes csr->vsstatus to CSR_VSSTATUS (VS-Status, not sstatus/mstatus). VCPU put reads CSR_VSSTATUS back into csr->vsstatus. This is proper virtualization — the guest's view of sstatus is managed through VSSTATUS, with no direct writes to the host's sstatus/mstatus bits 24/42 beyond what the trap save/restore already handles.
VCPU reset initializes sstatus to SR_SPP | SR_SPIE (0x120). Neither bit 24 nor bit 42 is set. This is a clean reset state with no TTCD-related bits asserted.

CPU suspend/resume saves CSR_STATUS to suspend context and restores it verbatim. No TTCD-specific handling. The suspend entry at line 48-49 reads the live CSR_STATUS (including any opaque bits at 24/42) and saves them; resume writes them back. This is correct opaque-state preservation.
findings.snippet:
.macro suspend_restore_csrs
  REG_L t0, (SUSPEND_CONTEXT_REGS + PT_EPC)(a0)
  csrw CSR_EPC, t0
  REG_L t0, (SUSPEND_CONTEXT_REGS + PT_STATUS)(a0)
  csrw CSR_STATUS, t0

findings.finding: Searched the full arch/riscv/ tree for 'TAG_CHECK', 'tag.elide', 'tagelide', 'nietc', 'SPTTCD', 'MPTTCD', 'TTCD', 'zitagelide', 'BIT(24)', 'BIT(42)' — zero matches in arch/riscv/. No code location references these bits. The kernel has no awareness of the removed zitagelide extension in any path (signal delivery, start_thread, ptrace, etc.).
findings.snippet:
/* grep for TTCD|TAG_CHECK_ELIDE|zitagelide|SPTTCD|MPTTCD|nietc|BIT(24)|BIT(42)
   across arch/riscv/ returned zero matches */

findings.finding: XTheadVector uses bits 23-24 of sstatus for VS status (SR_VS_CLEAN_THEAD=0x01000000, SR_VS_DIRTY_THEAD=0x01800000). Bit 24 (0x01000000) is the former SPTTCD position. On hardware that supports XTheadVector, bit 24 will be actively toggled by context-switch. This is NOT a TTCD violation — XTheadVector is a vendor extension with known semantics — but if future spec revisions repurpose bit 24 for a different mandatory feature, the XTheadVector usage at this bit position could conflict. Currently low risk since XTheadVector and zitagelide cannot coexist on the same hart.
findings.snippet:
#define SR_VS_THEAD      _AC(0x01800000, UL) /* xtheadvector Status */
#define SR_VS_OFF_THEAD   _AC(0x00000000, UL)
#define SR_VS_INITIAL_THEAD _AC(0x00800000, UL)
#define SR_VS_CLEAN_THEAD _AC(0x01000000, UL)
#define SR_VS_DIRTY_THEAD _AC(0x01800000, UL)
